description: Bank SMS/notification parsing rules for Buddy expense tracker. Used by both Dart and Kotlin parsers. India rules are documented here but India parsing in Kotlin uses hardcoded logic for performance and reliability. This file drives all other countries.

rules.description: India baseline — Kotlin uses hardcoded logic. This entry documents the patterns only.
rules.notes: Kotlin NotificationListener.kt uses its own hardcoded implementation for India. This entry is informational.

rules.description: Kuwait generic rules — KWD uses 3 decimal places
France — European decimal format with space thousands (1 234,56 €)
South Korea — KRW has 0 decimal places
Indonesia — IDR uses dot for thousands (Rp50.000 = 50,000 IDR), 0 decimal places
Singapore — DBS/POSB, OCBC, UOB, Grab, PayNow
rules.notes: Singapore banks primarily send SMS and in-app push. PayNow (instant transfer) uses SGD. Amount format: S$1,234.56.
